name: Iluvatar CoreX BI-V100 (Tiangai 100) / MR-V100 (Zhikai 100)
memory_bandwidth_basis: None available. Iluvatar publishes memory TYPE and CAPACITY on both cards - HBM2 32 GB on the BI-V100 training card, HBM2E 32 GB on the MR-V100 inference card - and the 16 GB HBM2E for the smaller MR-V50, but publishes NO bandwidth figure, no bus width and no compute throughput on either page. That is remarkable for a vendor product page: the memory capacity and the TDP are both stated, and the two numbers a roofline needs are both absent. Sources cn-iluvatar-tianggai100 and cn-iluvatar-zhikai100.
notes: THE HIERARCHY POINT: Iluvatar is worth a record despite publishing no compute or bandwidth figure, because it is doing something no other vendor in this slice is doing and it is doing it in a way that changes the inference economics. It is shipping HBM on INFERENCE-ONLY CARDS. The MR-V100 Zhikai 100 (released December 2022) is explicitly a general-GPU INFERENCE product with 32 GB of HBM2E at 150 W in a full-height full-length single-slot passive card, plus a 16 GB HBM2E variant (MR-V50 Zhikai 50) at 75 W in half-height half-length. Every other Chinese inference part in this repo is LPDDR - MLU370 at 307 GB/s, Ascend 310P at 204.8 GB/s, and even Moore Threads' S4000 at 768 GB/s on GDDR6 is not HBM. HBM2E at inference power and inference pricing is a genuinely different proposition, and it is the reason this record exists despite the missing numbers. THE BI-V100 TRAINING CARD is the other half: 7 nm, 32 GB HBM2, 250 W, released March 2021 after four years of development and billed as the first wholly domestic 7 nm GPGPU, in a full-height full-length dual-slot passive card with PCIe Gen4 x16. ITS INTERCONNECT SPEC IS THE MOST UNUSUAL NUMBER IN THIS ENTIRE SLICE: Iluvatar specifies 'shared 64 GB/s host bidirectional bandwidth' AND 'shared 64 GB/s device-to-device interconnect bandwidth' as the same figure, i.e. the card's internal link and its host link are symmetric at 64 GB/s. Whether those are truly one shared resource or two parallel ones is not stated, and the word 'shared' is doing ambiguous work in the vendor's own text - flagging it rather than resolving it. At 64 GB/s of device-to-device, scale-up is extremely weak, so BI-V100 multi-card work is effectively PCIe- and RoCE-bound. NO COMPUTE FIGURES ANYWHERE on either page; the vendor instead makes relative claims - 'industry-leading compute and energy efficiency', average performance across 100+ benchmark models 'comparable to mainstream products' on BI-V100, support for 200+ AI models, and on MR-V100 a claim of '2-3x the actual real-world performance of existing mainstream products' plus 50%+ reduction in migration time versus mainstream products and CUDA-ecosystem compatibility. None of these are measurable. Software is DeepSpark, an open community. VENDOR STATUS: founded end-2015 by Li Yunpeng (ten years at Oracle), unicorn valuation over USD 1bn in 2024, HKEX IPO 8 January 2026 (ticker 9903), strong government ties including the Shanghai Supercomputer Center. Worth noting the corporate turbulence: Diao Shijing was appointed chairman and CEO in May 2021 and taken away for investigation in an anti-graft probe in July 2022.
